declared.title: Choice Deprivation, Choice Overload, and Satisfaction with Choices Across Six Nations
declared.foundIn: rapport contre-preuve reports/too-many-choices/counter-evidence.md (2026-11-22), DOI trouvé par ses requêtes ; titre relevé sur Crossref par la session : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: 7,436 people in Brazil, China, India, Japan, Russia and the US, six domains of choice

findings.text: In most domains and most countries, people reported having less choice than they wanted; only in the US was having too much choice commonly reported

support.sentence: In most domains in most countries, choice deprivation was the norm-only in the United States was choice overload commonly reported.

findings.text: Having too little choice went with lower satisfaction with one's choices more strongly than having too much

support.sentence: Deprivation was also more strongly related to decreased satisfaction with choices than was overload, suggesting that choice deprivation can be both more common and more consequential than overload.

limits: self-reported, one survey: no causal order
no Arab country among the six
allegiance: co-authors Iyengar and Schwartz started the « too much choice » idea: here a finding against its generality
